rationale: One critical and two major findings block approval. CR-001 is the primary blocker: the async_pre_call_hook checks data.get('store') is False, but LiteLLM merges litellm_params (including store: false from the model entry) at route_request time — after async_pre_call_hook fires. The hook therefore never sees store=False from server-side model config, which is the documented primary trigger. The fix is only effective when the client explicitly sends store: false in the request body, leaving the original production scenario (model entry with litellm_params.store: false) unresolved. CR-002 is a secondary correctness issue: when all input items are reasoning items and get stripped, data['input'] becomes [], which Azure Responses API rejects with 400. CR-003 requires a product decision: id-only reasoning items ({type:reasoning, id:rs_xxx} without encrypted_content) are intentionally preserved by the filter, but it is unverified whether Azure also rejects these when store=False. No spec was supplied; confidence is low. One dismiss: TestResolvedDeployment 'stub' finding from blind lens was a false positive caused by abbreviated diff representation — actual tests have full assertions.

standards_review.notes: No commits on this branch yet; format cannot be checked.
async_pre_call_hook uses bare dict annotations (data: dict, -> dict) rather than dict[str, Any]. Consistent with pre-existing style in the same file; not blocking.
No secrets, no auth bypass, no injection surface introduced.

findings.title: store from server-side litellm_params never reaches data at hook time
findings.problem: data.get('store') is False only when the client explicitly sends store: false in the request body. When store: false is in litellm_params for a model entry (the documented primary trigger), LiteLLM merges that value at route_request time (common_request_processing.py:1179) — after async_pre_call_hook fires (line 943). The hook therefore never sees store=False from server-side model config.
findings.impact: The fix is inoperative for the primary documented use case. Turn-2+ Codex CLI requests still reach Azure with store=False (injected by the router) AND the encrypted_content reasoning items, causing the same 400 errors the hook was meant to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Move the stripping logic to a hook that fires after deployment selection (e.g. async_pre_call_hook_with_deployment if available in the installed LiteLLM version), or read the model's litellm_params from the deployment object rather than from data. A simpler alternative: strip encrypted_content reasoning items unconditionally whenever they appear in input, since they are always server-state-dependent and harmless to remove on models where store=true (they are still forwarded when present and the model was configured to store). Verify this approach against Azure behavior first.

findings.title: No guard when stripping reduces input to empty list
findings.problem: If every item in input is a reasoning item with encrypted_content, filtered becomes [] and data['input'] is set to []. The Azure Responses API rejects requests with an empty input array with a 400 error.
findings.impact: A session where the Codex CLI sends only reasoning items (e.g. session replay or multi-agent use) would change the error from '400: referenced item not found' to '400: input must not be empty', introducing a harder-to-diagnose failure mode caused by the hook itself.
findings.recommendation: Add a guard: only replace data['input'] if len(filtered) > 0. When filtered would be empty, leave data['input'] unchanged (surface the original 400) or log a warning and skip. Add a test case for the all-reasoning-items edge case.

findings.title: Id-only reasoning items not stripped — Azure behavior unverified
findings.problem: The filter requires both type=='reasoning' AND encrypted_content being truthy. Reasoning items that reference prior state only by ID — {'type':'reasoning','id':'rs_xxx'} without encrypted_content — pass through. It is unverified whether Azure also rejects these items with 400 when store=False.
findings.impact: If Azure rejects id-only reasoning items when store=False, the fix is incomplete: some turn-2+ requests will still fail after the hook runs, with non-obvious failure because other reasoning items were stripped but these were not.
findings.recommendation: Verify empirically: send an id-only reasoning item to Azure against a store=False model entry and check whether it returns 400. If it does, broaden the filter to strip all reasoning items regardless of encrypted_content: not (isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'reasoning'). The test test_preserves_reasoning_items_without_encrypted_content should then be updated with a comment citing the Azure API behavior.
